fullPassage: In fact, humans are known to have the largest and most visible sclera — the “whites” of the eyes — of any species. This fact intrigues scientists, because it would seem actually to be a considerable obstacle: imagine, for example, the classic war movie scene where the soldier dresses in camouflage and paints his face with green and brown color — but can do nothing about his noticeably white sclera, beaming bright against the jungle. There must be some reason humans developed it, despite its obvious costs. In fact, the advantage of visible sclera — so goes the “cooperative eye hypothesis” — is precisely that it enables humans to see clearly, and from a distance, which direction other humans are looking. Michael Tomasello showed in a 2007 study that chimpanzees, gorillas, and bonobos — our nearest cousins — follow the direction of each other’s heads, whereas human infants follow the direction of each other’s eyes. So the value of looking someone in the eye may in fact be something uniquely human.

ch: 인간의 보이는 공막이 지닌 진화적 이점과 협력적 기능

questions.passage: In fact, humans are known to have the largest and most visible sclera — the “whites” of the eyes — of any species. This fact intrigues scientists, because it would seem actually to be a considerable obstacle: imagine, for example, the classic war movie scene where the soldier dresses in camouflage and paints his face with green and brown color — but can do nothing about his noticeably white sclera, beaming bright against the jungle. There must be some reason humans developed it, despite its obvious costs. In fact, the advantage of visible sclera — so goes the “cooperative eye hypothesis” — is precisely that it enables humans to see clearly, and from a distance, which direction other humans are looking. Michael Tomasello showed in a 2007 study that chimpanzees, gorillas, and bonobos — our nearest cousins — follow the direction of each other’s heads, whereas human infants follow the direction of each other’s eyes. So the value of looking someone in the eye may in fact be something uniquely human.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 공막은 위장에 불리하지만, 시선 파악이라는 협력적 기능 덕분에 진화적으로 발달했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 인간의 큰 공막은 위장에 불리하지만, 타인의 시선을 파악하는 데 도움이 되는 협력적 진화의 산물이다 — 글의 전체 논리(비용→이점→가설→증거)를 정확히 요약 ←정답
❌ ② 영장류의 눈 구조는 종마다 다르며, 이는 각 종의 생존 전략을 반영한다 — 종별 눈 구조 비교는 글의 중심이 아님
❌ ③ 인간 유아가 시선을 따라가는 능력은 언어 발달 이전의 핵심적인 소통 수단이다 — 언어 발달은 글에서 언급되지 않음
❌ ④ 자연선택은 항상 생존에 유리한 형질만을 보존하므로, 공막의 발달은 필연적이었다 — '항상 유리한 형질만'은 글의 논지와 다름. 글은 비용에도 불구하고 이점이 있다는 구조
det.tip: obstacle(비용) + advantage(이점) = 비용-편익 구조. 협력적 눈 가설이 핵심
